newsitem.title: UK: SFA raps stockbrokers Pilling, expels former broker.
newsitem.headline: SFA raps stockbrokers Pilling, expels former broker.

text.p: British financial regulator the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Thursday it had disciplined private stockbroking firm Pilling & Co and expelled a former broker at the company for reckless trading for clients.

The broker, Norman Mauroo, "has been deemed to be not fit and proper to be registered with the SFA and has been expelled from the register of representatives and has been ordered to pay 6,000 stg towards costs," it said in a statement.
Pilling & Co has agreed to a settlement with the SFA and to a fine of 10,000 stg and 8,000 towards costs, it added.
The SFA said Mauroo, while working at Manchester-based Pilling's London branch, gave unsuitable investment advice and recommendations to its clients.

Other breaches included failing to obtain or keep adequate records of details of customers' financial circumstances and their investment objectives and causing them to enter into "intra account trades that were beyond their means".

Mauroo also advised customers to buy securities without having adequate knowledge about the relevant company and ignored instructions from one customer, the SFA said. "His trading on behalf of customers amounted to recklessness," it added.

The SFA said Mauroo had, in the case of one customer, obtained a cheque "obstensibly to purchase shares for that customer; the proceeds of the cheque were put towards a debit balance on Mauroo's personal dealing account at the firm".

It said Pilling & Co had admitted that for a period of almost 18 months between May 1993 and October 1994 it had failed to organise and control its internal affairs "in a responsible manner" by failing to have adequate arrangements to ensure its staff were properly trained and properly supervised.

The firm also admitted responsibility for Mauroo's actions in failing to ensure it did not make unsuitable personal recommendations to private customers and by failing to keep adequate records relating to private customers of the firm.
The SFA said Pilling & Co had notified it that it planned to close the London branch on November 1.
